To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spectroscopic factors deduced from nucleon transfer reactions are systematically reduced by 30% relative to shell-model values.

spectroscopic factors deduced from (d,p) reactions are suppressed relative to independent-particles shell-model predictions by {approx} 30% when the reaction model uses potential geometries constrained using Hartree-Fock wave functions.
the neutron spectroscopic factors obtained from ground-state to ground state (d,p) or (p,d) reactions are systematically reduced by 30% when using Hartree-Fock constrained potential geometries.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a systematic and consistent reaction theory for neutron transfer reactions, which we apply to the determination of neutron spectroscopic factors in light, medium, and heavy mass nuclei.
the development and application of a consistent three-body reaction model for neutron-transfer reactions.
the development of a systematic three-body model reaction theory for nucleon-transfer reactions, and the application of that theory to deduce spectroscopic factors from (d,p) reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spectroscopic factors deduced from nucleon transfer measurements are systematically reduced by {approx}20% to {approx}40% with respect to the large-basis shell model, which has been the standard for many decades, and which we believe is the most reliable model available for this type of calculation.
the spectroscopic factors deduced from (d,p) reactions are systematically suppressed by a factor {approx}0.7 with respect to the independent-particle model predictions.

the spectroscopic strength of nucleons in nuclei is reduced from that expected in a single-particle picture, by {approx}25-35% on average, for all the nuclei studied here and for the other nuclei studied in the literature, with the exception of the {sup 40,48}Ca and {sup 208}Pb nuclei, for which the spectroscopic strength is reduced by only {approx}10%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spectroscopic strengths for well-bound single-particle states, as measured in nucleon transfer and knockout reactions, are suppressed relative to independent-particles shell-model predictions.

the spectroscopic strength for nucleons from ground-state to groundstate reactions on well-bound targets is reduced by {approx} 30% relative to the independent-particle shell model, with the reduction increasing with increasing binding energy of the target.
the shell-model spectroscopic factors are systematically overestimated by {approx}40%.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the deduced spectroscopic strength from (d,p) reactions on calcium isotopes, and from (p,d) reactions on B, C, N, O, and F, are systematically lower than the independent particle shell-model predictions.

the neutron spectroscopic factors for well-bound nuclei are suppressed by {approximate}30% relative the independent-particle shell model, with the suppression increasing with the neutron separation energy.
the use of Hartree-Fock constrained reaction geometries leads to spectroscopic factors that are systematically smaller than independent-particle shell model predictions.
